transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I'm sure it's mostly just stress—being a chief executive, there's always a lot of pressure, you know? But... well, I came in because I've been having some, I guess, strange moments lately. I hope I explain this right. 

I keep... overhearing people talking about me. Usually the board members or my staff. I'll hear them right through the solid conference room walls, or... or even coming from my cell phone when it's completely turned off. They keep saying that I'm ruining the company. 

It's actually really embarrassing to admit this out loud, but it sounds so incredibly clear that I've been answering them back. And then I look around and realize... no one else heard it. I'm sorry, I know how that sounds. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here. Does it make sense that I'd come in for something like that?
How long have you been hearing these voices?

Um... well, if I really think about it, the ones coming from the walls, or when my phone is off... I guess that's been happening for about the past three months. 

I know I probably should have called to see someone sooner, and I'm so sorry if I let it go on too long. I just kept hoping it was a temporary thing, you know? Like maybe I just needed to catch up on my sleep and it would all just fade away. Three months isn't too terrible of a delay to come in, is it? I really hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
During this time, have you had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric?

No, not really. I mean, I'm a pretty energetic person in general—you kind of have to be to run a company—but I wouldn't say I've felt unusually high or euphoric. Mostly just... stressed, like I mentioned. And tired from not sleeping well. I hope that's the right answer. I'm not trying to hide anything, I just... I don't think I've felt anything like what you're describing. Is it okay that I haven't experienced that?
Do you believe anyone is deliberately trying to harm you or sabotage you?

Um... well, no, I don't think so. I mean, I know the corporate world can be cutthroat, and people get competitive, but... I don't really believe anyone is actively plotting against me or trying to hurt me. 

I know it probably sounds a little contradictory, since I mentioned hearing them say I'm ruining the company, but... I don't think they're doing it to be malicious. I think they're just... worried about the business, maybe? I really try to get along with everyone, and I'd hate to think anyone actually wanted to sabotage me. 

I hope that makes sense. Is it normal to hear those things but not feel like someone is actually out to get you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what's going on.
Over the past few months, have you found yourself becoming less interested in things you usually care about?

Well... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm slacking off or anything, because I really do care about my company and my family. But... 

I used to be the one driving every single idea, you know? I'd be the first one calling people after a big opening, just so energized. But lately... um, sometimes I just sit at my desk for hours, just kind of staring at the agenda. And I've been barely speaking to my husband or my staff. It's like I just feel... almost nothing about the work I used to absolutely love. 

I feel terrible admitting that. I know I should be more engaged, and I'm really trying, I promise. It's just been a bit harder lately. Is that... is that okay to admit? I hope you don't think I'm just giving up or being lazy.
Have you had any major medical illness or neurological problem recently?

Um... no, not at all. I haven't had any major medical issues or neurological problems, thank goodness. I try to take really good care of my health, you know? I get my regular check-ups, and everything always comes back perfectly fine. 

I mean, I've had the usual minor things like a cold here or there, but nothing serious. And definitely nothing neurological. My brain is... well, physically healthy, I'm sure of it. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to reassure you that I'm not dealing with any other illnesses on top of everything else. Is it helpful that I'm otherwise healthy?
During these past three months, have you had a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um... depressed? Oh, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I know I just said I've been a little less engaged with work and everything, but... I don't feel sad or down like that. 

I really try to keep a positive outlook, you know? Even with the stress of the company and... and the things I've been hearing, I try to just keep pushing forward. I definitely wouldn't use the word depressed. I get up, I go to the office, I do what I need to do... I'm still functioning, I promise. 

I just... I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around crying all day or anything like that, because I'm really not. I'm trying my best to hold it all together. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I don't feel depressed, even with everything else going on.
Have other people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense?

Oh... um, no. No one has said anything like that to me. I try to be very clear when I speak, especially because of my role at the company. I mean, communication is so important, right? 

I always make an effort to stay on track and be professional. Sometimes I might have a lot of thoughts going on at once—just because there's always so much to manage—but I don't think I jump around or confuse people. At least, I really hope I don't. 

If I ever did get a little sidetracked, I'm sure someone would have gently pointed it out, but my staff and my husband haven't mentioned anything like that. I always try to make sure I'm making perfect sense. Is that the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm communicating clearly with you right now, too.
Have you had times when your body felt stuck or frozen and you couldn't move or respond, even though you were awake?

Um... stuck or frozen? Oh, no, definitely not. I haven't experienced anything like that. 

I mean, sometimes I might pause for a moment if I'm deep in thought—just because I have so much on my plate with the company and everything—but I'm never actually frozen or unable to move. I'm always very active and responsive. I have to be, you know? People rely on me to make decisions quickly.

I try to keep myself moving and engaged throughout the day. I definitely wouldn't want anyone to think I'm just sitting around completely unresponsive. That sounds really frightening, actually, and I'm so glad I don't have to deal with that. I hope it's reassuring that my body is perfectly fine and under my control. I'm doing my best to stay sharp for you and for everyone else. Is it okay that I haven't had any problems like that?
Before these last three months, had you noticed any earlier changes in yourself—like becoming more withdrawn, less motivated, or having unusual experiences?

Um... well... I really don't want you to think I haven't been doing my job, because I always try my absolute hardest. But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, things have been sort of... building up for a while now. Not in a bad way! Just... a lot to manage. 

I think it's been about two years and four months. That was when we had the big company expansion and I was put in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. It was a huge honor, and I just wanted to make sure everything ran perfectly. So if I seemed a little... quieter, or maybe a bit less social back then, it was really just because I was so dedicated to the new role and making sure it succeeded. 

I promise I wasn't just giving up or losing motivation, and I definitely wouldn't say I was withdrawing. I was just working very, very hard. I hope it's alright that I've been so wrapped up in the company for that long? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate timeline I can. Am I explaining that okay?
From when you first noticed these changes in yourself up to today, has it been at least six months?

Oh, yes, definitely. Um... like I think I just mentioned a moment ago, it's been about two years and four months. You know, since the big company expansion when they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division? So, yes, it has been well over six months. 

But please don't think that means I've been doing a bad job for that long! It's really just that I've been so deeply focused on making the new division a success for all this time. I've been keeping everything running, I promise. It's just been building since then because the responsibilities are so important. 

Is that... does that give you the right timeframe for your paperwork? I want to make sure I'm answering exactly the way you need me to.
Have the voices ever happened during a time when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um... no, no, I wouldn't say that. I really don't want you to think I'm depressed or anything like that. I mean, everyone has a down day here and there, especially with the pressure I'm under at work, but I always make sure to keep a positive attitude. 

I definitely haven't felt sad or down most of the day for days on end. I try to stay really upbeat and keep the team motivated. The... the voices, they just happen while I'm working or, you know, going about my normal routine. But I'm not sitting around feeling depressed, I promise. I always try to keep a smile on my face and push through. 

Is it okay that I'm not feeling depressed? I hope that's a good thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression of how I handle things.
Apart from the voices, have you had a fixed belief that others would say is not true?

Um... no, definitely not. I mean, I know I'm under a lot of stress, but I'm very grounded in reality. I wouldn't want you to think I'm out of touch or making things up. 

I just focus on my work and try to do the best job I can for the company. I don't go around believing strange things or anything like that. I'm very rational, I promise. I always double-check my facts before making any big decisions for the division. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to reassure you that I'm completely clear-headed about everything else. I'm still doing a good job, right?
Compared with how you were before all this started, has your ability to function at work or in your relationships clearly gotten worse?

Um... well... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm failing or anything, because I really do try my best every single day. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, things have gotten a little... challenging. 

I wouldn't say "worse," exactly, just... different? Like at work, I'm still the chief executive of the division, but... well, I might not be quite as quick with some of the executive decisions as I used to be. The senior staff are so wonderful, though, they've just quietly stepped in to help out with some of the things I used to do myself. It's really just teamwork, you know? But I suppose I'm not running things quite as reliably as before. 

And at home... my husband is just an angel. He's been taking on a lot more of the household stuff lately. I sometimes start things and... well, I just don't always finish them. Or I might forget to start them at all. I feel terrible about it, I really do. 

Does that... is that okay to admit? I really hope you don't think less of me. I'm trying so hard to keep everything together, I promise.

Oh, yes, definitely. Um... like I think I just mentioned a moment ago, it's been about two years and four months. You know, since the big company expansion when they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division? So, yes, it has been well over six months. 

But please don't think that means I've been doing a bad job for that long! It's really just that I've been so deeply focused on making the new division a success for all this time. I've been keeping everything running, I promise. It's just been building since then because the responsibilities are so important. 

Is that... does that give you the right timeframe for your paperwork? I want to make sure I'm answering exactly the way you need me to.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have occurred only during mood episodes, to distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Have the voices ever happened during a time when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressive symptoms occurring concurrently with hallucinations (voices), which relates to a mood disorder or schizoaffective disorder. My symptom profile does not include information about depressive episodes or mood symptoms.

patient.answer:
Um... no, no, I wouldn't say that. I really don't want you to think I'm depressed or anything like that. I mean, everyone has a down day here and there, especially with the pressure I'm under at work, but I always make sure to keep a positive attitude. 

I definitely haven't felt sad or down most of the day for days on end. I try to stay really upbeat and keep the team motivated. The... the voices, they just happen while I'm working or, you know, going about my normal routine. But I'm not sitting around feeling depressed, I promise. I always try to keep a smile on my face and push through. 

Is it okay that I'm not feeling depressed? I hope that's a good thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression of how I handle things.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had delusions, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from unspecified nonorganic psychosis and clarify the breadth of psychotic symptoms.
doctor.question: Apart from the voices, have you had a fixed belief that others would say is not true?

patient.answer:
Um... no, definitely not. I mean, I know I'm under a lot of stress, but I'm very grounded in reality. I wouldn't want you to think I'm out of touch or making things up. 

I just focus on my work and try to do the best job I can for the company. I don't go around believing strange things or anything like that. I'm very rational, I promise. I always double-check my facts before making any big decisions for the division. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to reassure you that I'm completely clear-headed about everything else. I'm still doing a good job, right?

inference.note: Duration exceeds 6 months with at least 1 month of prominent hallucinations and negative symptoms, with no major depressive or manic episodes and no clear delusions/disorganization/catatonia. This supports schizophrenia over schizophreniform/brief psychosis, and argues against schizoaffective disorder.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is marked decline in work, self-care, or relationships from prior functioning, which helps distinguish schizophrenia from unspecified psychosis.
doctor.question: Compared with how you were before all this started, has your ability to function at work or in your relationships clearly gotten worse?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m no longer reliably able to run the division or keep up with basic executive decisions, and senior staff have quietly taken over work I used to handle myself. At home, my husband has had to manage most household responsibilities because I leave things unfinished or do not start them at all.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about the patient's ability to function at work or in relationships and whether it has clearly gotten worse compared to before the symptoms started. This matches the 'Functional Impairment' profile.

patient.answer:
Um... well... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm failing or anything, because I really do try my best every single day. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, things have gotten a little... challenging. 

I wouldn't say "worse," exactly, just... different? Like at work, I'm still the chief executive of the division, but... well, I might not be quite as quick with some of the executive decisions as I used to be. The senior staff are so wonderful, though, they've just quietly stepped in to help out with some of the things I used to do myself. It's really just teamwork, you know? But I suppose I'm not running things quite as reliably as before. 

And at home... my husband is just an angel. He's been taking on a lot more of the household stuff lately. I sometimes start things and... well, I just don't always finish them. Or I might forget to start them at all. I feel terrible about it, I really do. 

Does that... is that okay to admit? I really hope you don't think less of me. I'm trying so hard to keep everything together, I promise.

inference.note: Auditory hallucinations for 3 months plus >2 years of prodromal negative symptoms/functional decline, total duration >6 months, no major mood episodes, no clear medical cause, no disorganization/catatonia required. This rules out F29 and supports schizophrenia.

There is no evidence of manic or major depressive episodes coinciding with psychotic symptoms, no major medical/neurological condition identified, and no better-supported alternative psychotic disorder in the interview.
